text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.

- The top administrative body of the Christian Democratic Party has banned the so-called Barankovics group from formally operating within the party, while thye disciplinary committee expelled the mayor of the western city of Koszeg from the party and asked MP Denes Palfi to leave voluntarily.

- Hungary has reached a settlement with the four countries, Australia, Argentina, New Zealand and the US, that had filed a complaint with the World Trade Organisation over agricultural export subsidies. (Sat)

- The defense ministers and the chiefs of the general staffs of Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic, invited to join NATO, will hold consultations every three months during the period leading up to membership.

- The European Commission's study of EU associate members reportedly says that Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic are ahead of the other candidates, but most experts put the date of their admission at 2004.
- Hungarians have been extending help in restoring order following massive flooding in the Czech Republic, and Poland, and lesser damage in Slovakia.
- Unusual weather conditions have cost farmers nine billion forints in lost sales and damaged more than 100,000 hectares of crop.

- Shell Hungary Rt sold 50 percent of its annual target in the first half, and projects sales of 60 billion forints this year, 14.5 percent more than in 1996, marketing manager Csaba Orban told the newspaper.
- Both the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) and the Vienna-based economic research institute WIIW find that Hungary is bukcing the regional trend towards slower economic growth.

- Vilmos Apor, the Bishop of Gyor who died during Easter 1945 defending women and girls who had taken refuge in the bishopric fron drunken Russian troops, will be beatified by Pope John Paul II at a November 9 ceremony in the Vatican. (NEPSZABADSAG as well).
